Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Zimbabwe's reply. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Afghanistan players are need in a huddle, near the fence. Brian Bennett and Ben Curran open up for Zimbabwe. Yamin Ahmadzai has the new ball in hand. Let's go...
...SECOND INNINGS...

The success of the Zimbabwean bowling attack was primarily due to their pace bowlers. Brad Evans was exceptional, claiming a five-wicket haul, while Blessing Muzarabani provided excellent support by picking up three wickets. Tanaka Chivanga secured the important breakthrough, ending the vital second-wicket stand. Zimbabwe's batters will now aim to build a substantial lead to take a commanding position in the match. Stay tuned for the second innings.

A disastrous first innings for Afghanistan as they are bowled out for 127 runs. After losing Ibrahim Zadran early, a crucial 54-run partnership for the second wicket between Abdul Malik and Rahmanullah Gurbaz (who scored 37) provided a brief period of stability. However, following Gurbaz's dismissal, the Afghan batting order collapsed, with no other player making a significant contribution as wickets fell at regular intervals.

...DAY 1, SESSION 2...

However, the drinks break energized the hosts as the floodgates opened up with Afghanistan losing both the set batters inside a couple of overs. But the big moment in the session came when Zimbabwe got Afghanistan's skipper, Hashmatullah Shahidi cheaply. Zimbabwe have done a brilliant job after opting to bowl first. They have turned things around pretty quickly and have a chance to do more damage as Afghanistan have an inexperienced lower-middle order. Can the hosts clean up the visitors in the next session? Stay tuned to find out.

Zimbabwe have done a commendable job as they have pulled things back brilliantly in the final few minutes of the game, ending the session on a high. Afghanistan were happy to bat on a surface which was assisting the bowlers a bit. However, Afghanistan started well with Ibrahim Zadran setting the tone for his team with a couple of wonderful strokes. But his end was cut short by Blessing Muzarabani. Rahmanullah Gurbaz walked in and counterattacked, putting Zimbabwe under pressure as Afghanistan dominated until the first hour.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for action. The players are out in the middle. Ibrahim Zadran and Abdul Malik to open for Afghanistan. Richard Ngarava to bowl first. Three slips and a gully in place. Let's play...
The pitch report suggests there is a lot of green covering which will help the seamers. Time for the national anthems. It’s the national anthem of Afghanistan, followed by that of Zimbabwe.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Ibrahim Zadran, Abdul Malik, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Bahir Shah, Afsar Zazai (WK), Ismat Alam, Sharafuddin Ashraf, Khalil Gurbaz, Yamin Ahmadzai, Ziaur Rahman.
Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Ben Curran, Nick Welch, Brendan Taylor, Craig Ervine (C), Sikandar Raza, Tafadzwa Tsiga (WK), Brad Evans, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani, Tanaka Chivanga.

Hashmatullah Shahidi, the skipper of Afghanistan says they wanted to bat first as he feels there are some cracks which they think will start opening up as the Test match progresses. Reckons the debutant, Sharafuddin Ashraf, Khalil Gurbaz and Ziaur Rahman are talented guys. Admits they performed really well in domestic cricket and deserve to be here. Feels they need to be brave, take responsibilities and do the best for the team and enjoy the match.

Craig Ervine, the skipper of Zimbabwe says they want to bowl first as the pitch has a fair bit of green grass and also a bit of moisture. Tell they have a seam-heavy bowling option in the conditions which provide more bounce and pace than Bulawayo. Reckons that they had a tough year in terms of Test cricket but hopes they can get going here.
TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the toss and will BOWL first!

So, get ready for five days of exciting Test cricket! Will Afghanistan's strong batting and new-look bowling attack overcome the hosts? Or will Zimbabwe's mix of experience and exciting young talent finally secure a memorable win? The stage is set at the Harare Sports Club for what should be a closely contested and thrilling match. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Zimbabwe enters this contest missing one of their most experienced players, Sean Williams, and facing pressure to perform after a long winless streak in Test series dating back to 2011. The hosts will look to the seasoned heads of Brendan Taylor and captain Craig Ervine to guide the younger players. All-rounder Sikandar Raza is a key figure, and the team will rely heavily on promising youth like top-order batter Brian Bennett and the prolific Antum Naqvi, who could be in line for a debut. Zimbabwe needs their youngsters to rise to the occasion to secure a home victory.

For Afghanistan, this Test presents an opportunity for their emerging talent to step up. With senior stars like Rashid Khan and Mujeeb Ur Rahman unavailable, the spotlight shifts to lesser-known bowlers Bashir Ahmad and Zia-ur-Rehman. Their batting lineup looks strong and reliable, featuring the likes of Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, and captain Hashmatullah Shahidi. Keep an eye out for potential debutant, the handy all-rounder Sharafuddin Ashraf, but the visitors will surely miss the experience and runs of their injured stalwart, Rahmat Shah.

A fascinating one-off Test match is set to begin as Afghanistan takes on Zimbabwe at the Harare Sports Club! This game comes amidst a busy cricketing calendar and promises an engaging battle between two competitive sides. It's a chance for Afghanistan to build on their historic Test win against the same opponent earlier this year, while Zimbabwe will be eager to snap a long drought and register a much-needed Test series victory.
